bullets.text: Returned capital via $1.00 extraordinary dividend, $0.3987 variable dividend (Gainshare 1.50), and 13.3M share buybacks; retired $223M hybrid debt at 95% of par; debt-to-capital 24.5%; portfolio total return 7.8%.
Full-year CR 92.4; net income $1B; Direct calendar CR 94.6 with three months exceeding 96; Commercial Auto CR 87.5; 47 of 51 jurisdictions profitable, with PIP issues in large states addressed.

Redesigned UBI into Snapshot, simplifying marketing and lowering costs for agency and online rollout; unified Agency and Direct product architectures; believes Name Your Price tool contributed nicely to 2010 growth.

Added 750,000+ policyholders and over 1M customers in 2010; policy life expectancies reached all-time highs in both channels; closed in on 1M multi-product customers, with growing homeowners and renters bundles.

Flo remained central to advertising with nearly 2.5M Facebook fans; tested new customer-advocate character 'Messenger' in late 2010; hired Jeff Charney as Chief Marketing Officer to strengthen media and creative disciplines.

Transitioned from a 'transaction' to a 'destination' company by embedding a customer-care culture; prioritized renewal rate stability and loyalty programs; tracked progress via Net Promoter Scores with room for further improvement.

NPW rose 3.4% YOY to ~$14.5B; Direct achieved strong double-digit new application growth in Q1 and Q2; Agency auto production sustained attractive application and PIF expansion throughout the full year.

Direct emerged as an industry leader contributing significantly to growth; monthly Direct CR allowed to exceed 96 during high growth; Agency PIF rebounded near all-time highs with momentum expected to continue into 2011.

Decade reflected two distinct halves: rate-driven profitability and double-digit growth, followed by industrywide written premium declines; believes closing years mark the turn where sustained premium declines turn positive and profitability moderates.

Progressive earned 16 of 17 Keynote website awards; plans to exploit smartphones and tablets to expand product presentation; call centers began testing call diagnostics technology to evaluate customer interaction styles and stress.
